strength.sf_peak_min.measured_on: decided: a target for printed load paths; not measured
strength.sf_peak_min.description: peak safety factor: strength in the weakest case over the peak stress

strength.creep_share_max.description: sustained stress as a share of the wet strength

strength.wet_knockdown.measured_on: estimate for nylon blends, not measured
strength.wet_knockdown.description: share of the strength a nylon blend loses when wet

strength.torque_screws_min.description: least screws that carry torque between two printed parts

rules.title: A load-bearing part meets three criteria
rules.statement: A load-bearing printed part is sized for what its actuator can deliver and meets three criteria: a peak safety factor of {strength.sf_peak_min} in its weakest case (wet, with a share of {strength.wet_knockdown} of the strength lost, and across layers), a sustained stress under a share of {strength.creep_share_max} of the wet strength, and a stiffness limit. Every torque source is added. A load calculation names its pivot and its lever arm. No blanket oversizing.
rules.why: The torque of a build exceeded its capacity twice in early layouts. One load estimate used the wrong pivot.

attest.question: Load-bearing part: which load case sizes it, and does it meet the peak, creep and stiffness limits?
labels: sized for the actuator's peak: the calculation with its pivot and lever arm is in the report for the owner

rules.note: Deferred: no number typed by an agent is accepted as evidence; a judged calculation comes later.

rules.title: Layers run along the load
rules.statement: Layers run along bending members and no load path pulls across layers. A small shaft, stem, key or tang under torque is steel or lies flat. A lug loaded in bending gets a 45 deg gusset. A loaded pin is held at both ends and named by its strength class.
rules.why: The stem of a printed cam snapped on a layer line and its fork tangs broke. A frame printed upside down put its legs in tension across the layers and was split.

rules.title: Two features meant as one solid overlap for real
rules.statement: Two features meant to be one solid overlap by a real volume. The joint is verified before any stress number is trusted. A number from a paper study is measured again on the body.
rules.why: A stem overlapped its plate by about 0.5 mm: the quoted stress assumed material that was not there.

rules.title: A housing that carries load is held at both ends
rules.statement: A gearbox or motor housing that carries joint load is fastened at both ends. A link is carried on both sides of its actuator, so that the output bearing takes no tipping. Motors sit on the centre line between the links.
rules.why: No lost print is on record. A housing held at one end tips its bearing under load.

rules.title: An adjuster has a scale and stops
rules.statement: An adjuster has a scale, a hard stop at the target or a stated torque, and stops at both ends of its travel. A spring is checked for its stroke, not only for its force. Design around stock springs.
rules.why: On a built machine a spring could not be stretched onto its pin by hand.

rules.title: Torque goes through screws and stops, not a printed key
rules.statement: A clamped face that must hold an adjustable angle gets shallow serration on one side or prints on the textured plate. Torque between printed parts goes through at least {strength.torque_screws_min} screws and positive stops, never through a printed key.
rules.why: The printed key of an adjustable cam broke.
